name: motions-evil-ghostel
comment: evil-ghostel normal-state motions, text objects and insert-state key passthrough on zsh, complementing the operator matrix in shells.json (which is not repeated here). Motion groups assert point against the terminal cursor (j never passes the cursor's row, G returns to it, gg reaches the top, insert from a scrollback row lands at the prompt, ^ and $ hit the typed-input edges). Operator groups type a command, apply an Evil text object or motion operator, run it, and assert the output line -- the shell proves the edit landed. Passthrough groups drive the insert-state Ctrl and <delete> keys the same way. Every group starts in insert state at an empty prompt and uses its own marker text, so one failure does not cascade and a `wait text` cannot match stale output. Use --keep-going so every group reports.

steps.comment: short prompt, no right prompt; seed scrollback rows above the cursor
j cannot move below the terminal cursor's row: k k k then five j ends on the cursor row; a counted j from the top stops there too

steps.eval: (when (= (line-number-at-pos (point) t) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)) (error "J-SETUP k k k did not leave the cursor row: l%d" (line-number-at-pos (point) t)))

(unless (= (line-number-at-pos (point) t) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)) (error "J-CLAMP point=l%d cursor=l%d" (line-number-at-pos (point) t) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)))

(unless (= (line-number-at-pos (point) t) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)) (error "J-COUNT point=l%d cursor=l%d" (line-number-at-pos (point) t) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)))

steps.comment: G from scrollback returns to the live cursor; gg reaches the top of the buffer

steps.eval: (unless (and (= (line-number-at-pos (point) t) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)) (<= (1- ghostel--cursor-char-pos) (point) ghostel--cursor-char-pos)) (error "G point=%d/l%d cursor=%d/l%d" (point) (line-number-at-pos (point) t) ghostel--cursor-char-pos (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos t)))

steps.comment: k k i from a scrollback row types at the prompt, not at point
^ goes to the first typed character, past the prompt; x there deletes it
$ lands on the last typed character; i there inserts before it
ci" replaces the text inside double quotes
ci' replaces the text inside single quotes
di( empties a command substitution
dt<char> deletes up to, not including, the char
df<char> deletes through the char
d3w deletes three words
cb changes back to the previous word start
d^ deletes back to the input start
d0 stops at the input start instead of eating the prompt
yiw then a paste after the last character
u restores the deleted char (zle undo); C-r in normal state does not re-delete it, and says so

steps.eval: (unless (with-current-buffer "*Messages*" (save-excursion (goto-char (point-min)) (search-forward "Redo not supported" nil t))) (error "REDO-MSG not logged; echo=%S" (current-message)))

steps.comment: insert-state C-b and C-k: move back five, kill to end of line

steps.keys: C-b C-b C-b C-b C-b C-k

steps.comment: insert-state C-d on a non-empty line deletes the char under the cursor

steps.keys: C-a C-f C-f C-f C-f C-f C-d C-e

steps.comment: insert-state C-w then C-y: the killed word comes back from the zle kill ring
insert-state <delete> forward-deletes in the shell

steps.keys: C-a C-f C-f C-f C-f C-f <delete> C-e

steps.comment: insert-state C-t transposes the last two characters
insert-state C-p recalls the previous command
<up> recalls the previous command, <down> returns to the (empty) edit line
insert-state C-p then C-n: back to the empty line, so typing starts fresh
insert-state C-r reaches zle incremental search
insert-state TAB completes a file name in the shell
